## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Hetuduka, Kusalattika* is a text located in the *Duka-Tika-Paṭṭhāna* (Dyad-Triad) section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Nyanatiloka 2007]. The chapter systematically examines the conditional relations arising from the combination of the Root Dyad (*hetuduka*) and the Wholesome Triad (*kusalattika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In its positive formulas, it investigates permutations such as: dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and wholesome (*hetu kusala*), there arises conditioned by root condition (*hetupaccaya*) or other conditions, a phenomenon that is a root and wholesome, a phenomenon that is not a root but wholesome, or both [Nyanatiloka 2007]. It also applies negative interrogative permutations across these categories, such as the *nahetuduka-kusalattika* matrix [Nyanatiloka 2007].

No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit are recorded in SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 232 text-reuse matches across 53 other texts, reflecting the highly structured, formulaic nature of the *Paṭṭhāna*. The largest concentrations of shared textual material occur with other combinatorial sections of the work, principally *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1, 38 matches), *Hetuduka, Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 24.6, 12 matches), and structural cross-combinations such as *Hetuduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 9.1 and Patthana 15.1), *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1), and *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 22.1) [DharmaNexus].
